subject: HIPAA: audit log access, subpoena evidence, and BAA scope
body:
From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@clevelandclinic.org>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: audit@compaudit.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: audit logs & subpoena evidence (possible PHI)

Hi Jonas,

We received a preservation/subpoena request from our legal team that may require records of activity touching certain patient records (MRNs and timestamps) for a narrow set of user IDs that accessed our integration between Cleveland Clinic and your API in Oct-Nov 2026.

We need to understand whether Redwood can:
- Produce raw audit logs that include identifiers (timestamps, request IDs, tokenized user ids, and any request payload fragments) and whether those logs ever contain PHI from request bodies.
- Confirm retention windows for audit logs (hosted vs. dedicated) and the typical export format you can deliver for legal discovery.
- Outline redaction capabilities (server-side redaction or export-time masking) and an estimated turnaround for an export of ~6,000 matching log lines.

Attached is the initial subpoena notice (redacted). We also need documentation to satisfy our internal counsel: a one-page description of how Redwood treats request/response payloads in logs, and whether preservation would require a change in our BAA or additional scopes.

Please advise next steps and an ETA for a preliminary answer. We may need to scope a formal evidence request with your security team.

Thanks,
Maria Santos
Senior Paralegal — Legal Operations
Cleveland Clinic

Attachment: subpoena_notice.pdf (application/pdf, 192KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria.santos@clevelandclinic.org>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, audit@compaudit.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit logs & subpoena evidence (possible PHI)

Hi Maria — thanks for the detail and for sharing the notice. Looping in Dev (platform infra) and Laura (security & compliance) so we can provide a concise, defensible response.

Short answers up front (high-level):
- Do our logs ever contain PHI? Not by design. We do not log full request bodies for hosted customers by default; however, certain fields can be captured in structured request metadata (e.g., request_id, client_id, model, token counts, timestamps). For customers using our Dedicated/private deployments, customers sometimes enable elevated debug logging for troubleshooting which could capture request fragments — that needs to be checked per deployment.
- Retention windows: Standard hosted audit logs are retained for 90 days by default (extendable with paid retention), Dedicated environments can be configured per contract (we've seen 1–7 years).
- Export and redaction: We can export logs in CSV/JSONL; we offer export-time redaction (pattern-based masking) and a one-off field-level redaction service with an engineering runbook.

Next steps from our side:
1) Dev will confirm whether Cleveland Clinic's tenant had debug logging enabled during the timeframe in question (Oct–Nov 2026).
2) Security will provide a one-page evidence summary describing logging scope, where we persist telemetry, and how PHI is handled under our BAA.
3) If raw payload fragments are present and contain PHI, we will propose redaction and minimal-export options or route to a Dedicated-data export process.

I attached a preliminary inventory template to capture what records you need; please fill the columns you can and return — it will speed the legal discovery workflow.

Action items: Dev to check debug flags & provide sample log schema; Laura to draft evidence one-pager and list of contractual implications.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partner Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: requested_evidence_inventory.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 24KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 14:28:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: audit logs & subpoena evidence (possible PHI)

Forwarding Maria's notice and preliminary notes from infra.

On checking tenant settings and our internal telemetry:
- Tenant: cleveland-clinic-prod (tenant id: redacted for thread)
- Debug logging: NOT enabled on hosted path for Oct–Nov 2026 — we verified the flag across the cluster.
- Request bodies: hosted API ingestion pipeline strips request bodies from our long-term audit index (we persist minimal request metadata to the audit index and a short-lived request payload cache for 72 hours for troubleshooting). The payload cache is rotated and not part of standard exports.
- We do persist request hashes and a truncated prefix (up to 256 bytes) in ephemeral debug artifacts if debug is enabled; not applicable here.

Export options and estimates if legal insists on matching rows:
- Option A (fast): Export metadata-only logs (timestamps, request_id, client_id, route, token counts) — ~48–72 hours, deliver CSV. No PHI expected.
- Option B (thorough): Recover short-lived payload cache for the date range (if available) and run redaction patterns (MRN, DOB, PHI regex) before export — ~7–10 business days and requires signed evidence-handling SOP and scoped engineer time.
- Option C (if records not available): Formal forensic engagement via our partner ComplianceAudit Inc. to attempt deeper recovery — timeline depends on stateful snapshots and could be multi-week plus fees.

I'll prepare sample CSV schema and a short runbook for redaction patterns. Laura — can you confirm whether delivering Option B would require a BAA change or if it's covered by the existing BAA clause on "access to telemetry"?

- Dev

Attachment: redaction-options-summary.docx (application/msword, 12KB)

From: Maria Santos <maria.santos@clevelandclinic.org>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: audit@compaudit.com
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit logs & subpoena evidence (possible PHI)

Thanks, Jonas & Dev — that is helpful and clarifies the immediate technical posture.

We will do the following:
- Complete the inventory you attached (I will return by EOD Thu 12/24).
- For now, please provision Option A export (metadata-only) as a first pass; our counsel will review and confirm whether we'll request Option B. If we move to Option B, we understand there will be an engineering run and an evidence-handling SOP.
- Please send the one-page evidence summary and a copy of the current BAA excerpt that covers telemetry/logging for our counsel to review.

Question for Redwood legal/compliance: is there a standard non-disclosure chain-of-custody template you use when we request redacted exports that still conceivably contain PHI? If so, please share.

Appreciate the quick response — attaching the (redacted) subpoena notice for your records.

Best,
Maria
Senior Paralegal — Legal Operations
Cleveland Clinic

Attachment: subpoena_notice.pdf (application/pdf, 192KB)
